name: Brackwater Dye Cropped Hoodie
description:
A cropped pullover hoodie in a heavyweight French terry cotton-synth blend, dyed using an acid-wash process that produces organic, unrepeatable streaks of color — each one genuinely unique. The base colors run toward industrial: rust, petroleum blue, chemical yellow, tar black. The crop hits at the natural waist, and the oversized hood has a wide drawstring in contrasting cord. The front kangaroo pocket is deep and reinforced at the seams. The cuffs are ribbed and slightly flared.

Brackwater is a street label run by a small collective in the Tier 1-2 borderzone, dyeing in small batches using reclaimed industrial chemicals and repurposed textile equipment. The process is not precisely safe and the results are not precisely consistent — which is entirely the point. They sell at market stalls, through a few sympathetic Tier 2 boutiques, and via a rotating contact list. The hoodie has become a minor status signal in Shelf-adjacent street culture: you know where to find it, or you don't.
what_it_says: You know people. You know where things come from. You're not trying to look like you bought this somewhere clean.
story_hooks: The dyeing chemicals Brackwater uses come from a specific industrial supplier — a supplier who may be connected to something considerably darker than textile production.
Two people wearing Brackwater hoodies from the same batch run into each other and realize the dye patterns, when held side by side, form a map.
A corponation's trend-forecasting division has flagged Brackwater as a target for acquisition or dissolution — the collective received the leaked report anonymously.

physical_description.visual_profile: A cropped pullover hoodie with an oversized, slightly slouched silhouette. The acid-wash dye creates organic, streaking patterns across the surface—no two are identical. Wide drawstring hood dominates the top half; deep kangaroo pocket anchors the front. Sits at natural waist, exposing a finger-width of skin between hem and pants. Reads as intentionally undone and street-forward.
physical_description.fit: Oversized through the body with a relaxed drop-shoulder cut. Cropped length hits precisely at the natural waist. Hood is roomy and sits naturally when worn up. Ribbed cuffs are slightly flared at the wrist, giving a subtle bell-mouth finish.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavyweight French terry cotton-synth blend—durable, breathable, slightly stiff when new but softens with wear. The blend resists pilling and synthetic fibers add longevity.
physical_description.texture: Fuzzy, napped terry surface on the inside; slightly smoother outer face. Acid-wash creates visual texture variation across the fabric—some areas appear faded or chemically burned, others retain deeper color saturation. Drawstring is a heavy contrast cord with visible knots.
physical_description.color_scheme: Base palette of industrial hues: rust orange, petroleum blue, chemical yellow, and tar black, combined in streaked, organic patterns. No two pieces identical. Drawstring typically runs in high-contrast color (cream, bright white, or acid green).
physical_description.closures: Pullover construction with drawstring hood adjustment. Front kangaroo pocket is open-access, reinforced at seams with visible stitching.
distinctive_features: Hand-acid-washed finish—genuinely unrepeatable color patterns on each piece
Deep, reinforced kangaroo pocket with contrast stitching
Wide, oversized hood with heavy contrast drawstring and visible knots
No visible branding or logos—authenticity signal is in the dye work itself
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 borderzone prestige—affordable street luxury. Signals awareness and insider access rather than wealth.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by street culture figures, creative class, and Shelf-adjacent communities who value independent manufacture and chemical aesthetics. Signals anti-corporate sensibility and knowledge of underground textile collectives. Distinctly not corpo.
physical_description.condition_typical: Breaks in quickly; raw edges soften, drawstring frays slightly, acid-wash patterns may blur with repeated washing. This degradation is considered character, not damage. Often worn with visible creasing and pilling on high-contact areas.
